questions.text: According to the ______ view of concepts, people categorize new instances by comparing them to representations of previously stored instances[cite: 5].
According to the typicality effect, the statement “A dog is a household pet” should be verified[cite: 13]:
options: Faster than “a poodle is a household pet”
Faster than “a dog is a living thing”
Faster than “a ferret is a household pet”
Faster than “a dog is an animal”
questions.correctAnswer: Faster than “a ferret is a household pet”

questions.text: Which of the following would be considered an example of a “natural kind” concept? [cite: 21]
A schema for a routine event, such as going to the dentist, is called a: [cite: 29]
A ________ is a mental representation of some object, event, or pattern. [cite: 37]
A ______ can be defined as a class of similar things that share either an essential core, or some similarity in perceptual, biological, or functional properties. [cite: 45]
Which of the following is NOT TRUE of the classical view of concepts? [cite: 53]
options: It proposes that concepts are mentally represented by list of features.
It assumes that membership in a category is clear-cut.
It accurately predicts the typicality effect.
‘Necessity’ and ‘sufficient’ features play an important role in the theory.
questions.correctAnswer: It accurately predicts the typicality effect.
